errors: No mention of QoS or bandwidth prioritisation for Engineering's heavy internal traffic, which was explicitly called out in the scenario
ACL policy for Finance is stated in general terms without specifying which protocols or services are permitted, making the 'strict access control' requirement only partially addressed
No mention of how the management VLAN is secured (e.g., restricting access to only authorized management hosts, or using a dedicated management interface on switches).
No mention of Spanning Tree Protocol considerations or how dual uplinks interact with STP (e.g., PortFast, BPDU Guard, or using LACP to avoid loops).
ACLs are mentioned generically but no indication of where they are applied (inbound/outbound on which interface) or what specific traffic is permitted/denied for Finance.
No internal network segmentation means lateral movement is possible after initial compromise
No least privilege or access control model means compromised credentials grant excessive access
No monitoring or logging means intrusions go undetected
Public website is not explicitly isolated (e.g., DMZ) from internal application servers
No internal network segmentation (e.g., VLANs, zones) to limit lateral movement
No mention of least privilege or role-based access control for internal apps
No monitoring, logging, or alerting (SIEM, IDS/IPS, audit logs) to detect breaches
